explain.say: Put your hand on your chest. Can you feel your heart beat? It is steady. Music has a steady beat too. Look at the board. One side shows the pulse. The other side shows the rhythm.

explain.say: You can find a rhythm by clapping syllables. A syllable is a beat inside a word. Look at the board: wa, ter, mel, on. Watermelon has 4 claps. How many claps are in your name?
The pulse stays steady. The rhythm changes on top of it. Drummers all over the world play rhythms over a steady pulse. Try this. March the pulse with your feet. Clap watermelon with your hands.

faq.q: What is a pulse in music?
faq.a: The pulse is the steady beat that runs through a piece of music, like a heartbeat. Every beat is the same length, and it is what you march, tap or dance to.
asks: What is the beat in music?

faq.a: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds in music. It often follows the words of a song and changes as the song goes on.
asks: How do I clap a rhythm?

faq.q: What is the difference between pulse and rhythm?
faq.a: The pulse is steady and never changes its pattern; the rhythm is the mix of long and short sounds played on top of it.
asks: Is the beat the same as the rhythm?

faq.a: Tempo is how fast the pulse goes, measured in beats per minute. A slow lullaby might be 60 beats a minute and a lively dance 120 or more.

faq.q: How can I practise pulse and rhythm?
faq.a: Tap a steady pulse with your foot while clapping the rhythm of words or a song with your hands. Start slowly and speed up when it feels easy.
asks: How do I keep a steady beat?

facts: Tempo is measured in beats per minute (BPM).
A resting heart in an adult usually beats between 60 and 100 times a minute.

quiz.say: You tap your foot to a song. Every tap is the same. What are you tapping?
quiz.show: 🦶 The same steady tap. What is it?
quiz.why: The pulse is the steady beat. It stays the same all through the song.

wrong.1: Rhythm has long and short sounds, so it changes.
wrong.2: The words follow the rhythm. Your steady tap follows the pulse.

quiz.say: Say the word banana. Clap each part. How many claps?
quiz.why: Ba, na, na. That is 3 syllables, so 3 claps.

wrong.1: Say it slowly: ba, na, na. There is 1 more part.
wrong.2: Banana has 6 letters. Clap the parts you say, not the letters.
